headline: Is he being honest with you?
note:
⛔ The decode-him DECK was retired 2026-08-19 (operator call) — its strip art was the fb-palm thumb image and no ad ever pointed at it. Its block has been removed from this draft; the arcana and return-mhf decks are unaffected.

🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why. 🔴 THIS FAMILY WAS DELIBERATELY NOT LOOSENED: cut 3 still answers her FEAR (am I short of sense, or short of facts) and never rules on him in either direction. The art line and the bridge are unchanged.

Lives on ALL FOUR decks — three card-sets: Magician/Hanged Man/Fool (return-mhf + arcana-mfh, one copy, verb swapped), Emperor/Empress/Fool (arcana-eef), Sun/Moon/Tower (decode-him). The arcana-eef Fool reuses the MHF Fool copy verb-swapped, which is what the live registry already does for this hook.

🔴 decode-him takes NO picture line. Its strip art is the fb-PALM thumb image and there is no revealStrip, so there is no card for her to look at — beat 1 uses the card-name form instead, exactly as the already-shipped cards-feels and cards-return do on that deck. Every beat 1 here is written FRESH: all four decode-him hooks currently open with the SAME line per card and no guard file catches it.

🔴 NEVER ACQUIT HIM AND NEVER CONVICT HIM. TAROT_HOOK_TENDENCY: 'never state he is lying or that he is honest as fact; affirm HER instrument'. The VOC makes that a safety rule rather than a style rule — 28 real concerns off this exact lander, and a large share of them have never met the man: 'I just want make sure he is not an impostor', 'he says he loves me... I haven't met him afraid he's a scammer', 'I met this guy online. He's from Nigeria... my gut feeling tells me he's not [coming]'. A line that vouches for him could cost one of these women money. So every beat 3 certifies HER NOTICING and names what she was never given — never a verdict in either direction.

The accusation the absolution refuses is hers from the VOC too: 'Left confused doubting our entire relationship with no answers', 'I don't know if I can trust him'. She has been told she is distrustful. She is short of facts.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — he looks straight out at you, and his mouth is closed.
You asked if he's being honest with you. Your hand went to the man who tells it well.
So what you're short of is a fact, dear. Not sense, and not calm.
And look how he holds himself. He's very good at how a thing is put.
But a smooth account isn't proof either way, dear.
That's why his answers land fine, dear, and you still go back over them.
Let me look closer at what stands between you and the whole story…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — the whole card is upright but him.
You asked if he's being honest with you. Your hand went to the card that shows one side.
So you've only ever had one side of this, dear. The card is blunt about that.
And the other side of it sits with him, dear. It always has.
But you can't weigh a thing you were never shown, dear.
That's why he explains it, dear, and an hour later you're still checking.
Let me look closer at what's keeping the other side out of view…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — a small white dog up on its back legs beside him.
You asked if he's being honest with you. Your hand went to the one still on the road.
So this story isn't finished, dear. Nothing about it has been closed.
And look at the little dog, dear. Up on its back legs, trying to tell him.
But a warning with no words in it is all you've had, dear.
That's why you ask again in a good week, dear, when nothing has gone wrong.
Let me look closer at what has been standing in the way of the truth…

a: You chose the Emperor, dear. Look — armour on his legs, and a stone chair he doesn't leave.
You asked if he's being honest with you. Your hand went to the man who states things.
So you've had rulings from him, dear, and no reasons to go with them.
And a man on a stone chair doesn't explain himself much.
But a firm answer isn't the same as a full one, dear.
That's why you stopped asking twice, dear. The first answer closed the door.
Let me look closer at what sits between you and the real reason…
b: You chose the Empress, dear. Look — a field of wheat at her feet, and trees behind her.
You asked if he's being honest with you. Your hand went to the softest card in this deck.
So the warmth was real, dear. That much this card will give you.
And look at the wheat, dear. You can't see the ground through it.
But feeling loved and being told the facts are two different things.
That's why the evening can be lovely, dear. You still don't know where you stand.
Let me look closer at what stands between you and the plain facts…
